text.p: A national wage deal being negotiated with public sector workers would probably result in salary rises "slightly above" 2.5 percent, Prime Minister Antonio Guterres said in an interview.
The government has so far offered 2.375 percent, the mid-point of its 2.25-2.50 inflation forecast for next year.
But unions representing over 500,000 public sector employees, whose salary deals are usually a benchmark for the private sector, are seeking at least 4.5 percent.
In an interview with the state RTP channel on Wednesday night, Guterres said the rise would be "slightly above 2.5 percent."
Economists say anything above 3.0 percent could jeopardise the government's objective of seeing Portugal qualify for the European Union's single currency at its launch in 1999.
Guterres reaffirmed that his minority government would not accept any parliamentary ammendments to its budget package that threatened the deficit target.
He said the target of a 2.9 percent budget deficit to GDP ratio, just inside the 3.0 percent target for joining the single currency, left little margin for manoeuvre.
The government, which has 112 seats in the 230-seat parliament, has sent the budget plan to the legislature. The first debate is scheduled for November 13.
